Task: build the live-mode HTTP layer. Create ONLY: src/server/live/handlers.ts, src/app/api/live/_lib/runtime.ts, src/app/api/live/run/route.ts, src/app/api/live/status/route.ts, tests/live/handlers.test.ts. You may edit src/server/live/config.ts only if strictly necessary (tell me exactly why). Do not modify any other existing file. Never read .env or print environment variables, connection strings or keys. No network or database calls in tests. First read: src/server/live/* (especially run-live.ts, config.ts, store.ts, pg-store.ts, codes.ts, validate.ts), src/app/results/_lib/presentation.ts and synthetic-run.ts (read only), and how Next.js route handlers are already used in this repo (if at all).

handlers.ts (pure, no process.env, no src/app imports): export createLiveHandlers(runtime) returning { POST(request: Request): Promise<Response>, GET(request: Request): Promise<Response> }, where runtime = { getDeps(): Promise<LiveDeps | null> (null means the database or secret is not configured), getStore(): Promise<LiveStore | null> }.
POST: (1) reject a body larger than 4096 bytes (check Content-Length and the actual text length) or a non-JSON content type with 400 { status: "invalid_request", field: "code", message } using the fixed message style of run-live; invalid JSON gives the same 400; (2) derive the client ip: first the x-real-ip header, else the first element of x-forwarded-for, else the literal "unknown"; trim it and cap it at 64 chars (add a comment that this is trustworthy only behind a platform that sets these headers itself, such as Vercel, and that I have not verified Vercel's overwrite behaviour); (3) call runLive(body, ip, deps); if getDeps() returns null or throws, answer with liveUnavailable() from run-live.ts; (4) return Response.json(outcome.body, { status: outcome.httpStatus }) with headers Cache-Control: no-store, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Robots-Tag: noindex. Never log. Never include thrown error text in any response. Any unexpected exception gives liveUnavailable().
GET: returns 200 { enabled: boolean } from store.isLiveEnabled(), with the same headers; any store failure or null store gives 503 { status: "live_unavailable", message } (fixed message); rate limit it with store.hit("status:" + hashIp(ip, secret), now, 60, 60) like the run route uses its buckets, and a denied hit gives 429 { status: "rate_limited", retryAfterSeconds }.
Both handlers answer unsupported methods through Next's defaults (do not export other methods).

runtime.ts (server-only: import "server-only"): the default wiring. It reads configuration ONLY through readLiveConfig(process.env); memoizes the connected store in a module-level promise, but if connecting fails it clears the memo so the next request retries (never cache a rejection); builds LiveDeps with realFactories and now: () => new Date(). Required for any service: DATABASE_URL and INVITE_HMAC_SECRET; missing means getDeps() resolves null. The live keys (Crustdata and model) are optional: if they are missing, deps.live is null. IMPORTANT FAIL-SAFE: define const LIVE_RESULTS_MAPPER: ToResults | null = null with a comment saying a live-safe results mapper (not toResultsDto, which hard-codes synthetic facts) must exist before live runs are allowed; deps.live must be null whenever LIVE_RESULTS_MAPPER is null, regardless of the environment, so live runs can never spend money before a truthful mapper exists. deps.toResults is: for synthetic, toResultsDto from src/app/results/_lib/presentation (truthful for synthetic runs); for live, LIVE_RESULTS_MAPPER, and if it is null the function throws (never reached because live is null, but it must fail closed).
route.ts files: each is thin: import createLiveHandlers and the runtime, export POST (run) and GET (status) built from them, plus export const runtime = "nodejs"; export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"; and in run/route.ts export const maxDuration = 300 as a plain numeric literal (Next reads it statically). No logic in the route files.

Tests (tests/live/handlers.test.ts), with fakes only: oversized body gives 400; invalid JSON gives 400; wrong content type gives 400; ip is taken from x-real-ip, then x-forwarded-for first element, then "unknown" (assert through the bucket name passed to a fake store.hit using the hashed ip); every response carries the three headers; getDeps null or throwing gives 503 live_unavailable with the fixed body; a thrown error text never appears in a response; GET returns { enabled } and 503 on store failure and 429 when the hit is denied; the runtime fail-safe: with every env var set for live but LIVE_RESULTS_MAPPER null, a live-mode code is given the run back and no live factory is ever called (inject fakes to prove it); the memo clears after a failed connect (test this part through an exported pure helper createMemoizedConnector(connect) in handlers.ts or runtime.ts).
Run npx vitest run, npx tsc --noEmit, npm run lint, and npm run build (the build must still list /live and /results and now also /api/live/run and /api/live/status as dynamic routes). End with a plain-text SHORT REVIEW REPORT block (under 45 lines, no code fences, no secrets, no company data): the exports; the HTTP status per outcome; how the ip is derived; how the fail-safe works and where; every environment variable NAME read and which are required versus optional; the test names; the vitest, tsc, lint and build results as one line each; anything you changed outside the listed files; and anything you were unsure about.
</pasted_content id="01db">

content.text:
SHORT REVIEW REPORT

Exports
- handlers.ts: createLiveHandlers(runtime) returning { POST, GET }. It also exports createMemoizedConnector, clientIp and the LiveRuntime type.
- runtime.ts: runtime (getDeps, getStore), LIVE_RESULTS_MAPPER (null), and buildLiveDeps(config, store, mapper = LIVE_RESULTS_MAPPER). I added buildLiveDeps so the fail-safe can be tested without the environment.
- run/route.ts: POST, runtime = "nodejs", dynamic = "force-dynamic", maxDuration = 300.
- status/route.ts: GET, runtime = "nodejs", dynamic = "force-dynamic".

HTTP status per outcome
- POST body or content-type problems (over 4096 bytes, bad JSON, non-JSON content type, a body that is not an object): 400 invalid_request, field "code".
- runLive outcomes pass through as run-live defines them: 200, 400, 401, 403, 409, 429, 502, 503.
- getDeps null or throwing, or any unexpected exception: 503 live_unavailable, fixed message.
- GET: 200 { enabled }, 429 rate_limited with retryAfterSeconds, 503 live_unavailable.
- All responses carry Cache-Control: no-store, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and X-Robots-Tag: noindex.

IP derivation
- x-real-ip (trimmed), else the first x-forwarded-for element (trimmed), else "unknown". The result is capped at 64 characters.
- The code comment says this is trustworthy only behind a platform that sets the headers itself, and that I have not verified Vercel's overwrite behaviour.

Fail-safe
- LIVE_RESULTS_MAPPER is null in runtime.ts, and buildLiveDeps sets deps.live to null whenever the mapper is null, whatever the environment says.
- deps.toResults uses toResultsDto for synthetic runs. For live runs it uses the mapper, and throws if the mapper is null.
- With live null, runLive gives a live-mode code's run back and returns 502 run_failed, without calling a live factory.

Environment variable names read (only through readLiveConfig(process.env))
- Required: DATABASE_URL, INVITE_HMAC_SECRET. If either is missing, getDeps resolves null.
- Optional: CRUSTDATA_LIVE_API_KEY, LIVE_LLM_API_KEY, LIVE_LLM_BASE_URL. If any is missing, deps.live is null.

Tests (tests/live/handlers.test.ts)
- POST: rejects an oversized body with 400; rejects an oversized Content-Length with 400; rejects invalid JSON with 400; rejects a wrong content type with 400; derives the ip from x-real-ip, then x-forwarded-for, then unknown; carries the three headers on success and failure; answers 503 live_unavailable when getDeps is null or throws; never puts thrown error text in a response.
- GET: returns { enabled }; answers 503 on store failure or a null store; answers 429 when the status hit is denied.
- Other: runtime fail-safe (never calls a live factory while LIVE_RESULTS_MAPPER is null); createMemoizedConnector memoizes success and clears the memo after a failed connect.

Results
- vitest: 648 passed, 6 skipped, 0 failed (40 files passed, 1 skipped).
- tsc --noEmit: clean.
- lint: clean.
- build: succeeded. The routes are /, /live (static), /results (dynamic), /api/live/run and /api/live/status (dynamic).

Changed outside the listed files
- Nothing. config.ts is untouched and no other existing file was modified.
- git status shows only the new files.

Unsure about
- GET calls both getStore (for the store) and getDeps (for hmacSecret and now), because the runtime shape you specified has no other source for the secret. Either one returning null gives 503. Both read the same memoized connection.
- The route files assign the handlers to a const and then export POST or GET, rather than destructuring in the export. Next's static analysis of destructured exports was unclear to me.
- The runtime test uses vi.mock("server-only") because the real package throws outside Next's server build.
- A request without a Content-Length header is read in full before the 4096-byte check. The body is bounded only after reading, not while streaming.
